SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Progressive shortness of breath over ≈2 weeks, notably worse in the last few days; now breathless with minimal exertion (e.g., walking to shops, around house).
- Associated symptoms: Mild dry cough; bilateral ankle swelling for a few days; feels “run-down.” Denies chest pain, palpitations, fever, dizziness, or change in appetite/urination (baseline polyuria attributed to diuretics).
- Past medical history: 
  • Congestive heart failure  
  • Prior myocardial infarction (“small heart attack”) ≈5 years ago
- Medications: 
  • Furosemide – dose/frequency not documented (currently 1 tablet daily per context)  
  • Aspirin – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • Bisoprolol – dose/route/frequency not documented
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social history: Lives alone with two cats; part-time lorry driver (day shifts); ex-smoker (≈1 pack/day for 25 years, quit); no alcohol; limited exercise (walks to shops daily).
- Family history: Father died of heart attack in early 60s; mother alive with osteoporosis.

Objective:
- General: Appears well on video consult.
- Cardiovascular/Respiratory: Clinician reports chest examination normal; oxygen saturations and blood pressure within normal limits (exact values not provided).
- Extremities: Bilateral ankle edema (patient-reported).
- Investigations today: None performed during consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Worsening dyspnea & peripheral edema in known heart failure
   - Assessment: Likely acute exacerbation of chronic congestive heart failure.
   - Differential diagnosis: Anemia, pulmonary infection, pulmonary embolism (less likely given afebrile, no chest pain); conflict not indicated by transcript.
   - Investigations planned: 
     • Blood tests – full blood count, renal function/electrolytes.  
     • Echocardiogram to reassess ventricular function (to be scheduled within 1–2 weeks).
   - Treatment planned: Increase Furosemide from current regimen to 1 tablet twice daily (exact dose not documented); continue other heart-failure medications unchanged.
   - Follow-up: Review in 1 week; earlier contact advised for worsening breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.

Quality checks:

• Missing/expected elements:
  – Exact vital signs (BP, HR, SpO₂, weight) and physical findings (JVP, lung auscultation details).  
  – Current doses/strengths of Furosemide, Aspirin, Bisoprolol.  
  – Complete medication reconciliation (other possible cardiac drugs not discussed).  
  – Allergy status confirmed; immunization status not addressed.

• Internal conflicts: None noted.

• Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional connectivity issues but clinical content understandable.
